title: Finite smooth-point pinching on curves proper over a reference scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $S$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $s:X\to S$ be a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that $(X,\varnothing)$ is a semistable multipointed $k$-curve [def-trf-multipointed-curve, def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification]. Let $E\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], all in the smooth locus of $X/k$. Let $F$ be another finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $a:E\to F$ be surjective with every fibre having either one or two points, and supply $b:F\to S$ with $s|_E=ba$. The empty case $E=F=\varnothing$ is allowed. Then the scheme pushout $Y=X\amalg_E F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] exists; its map $v:X\to Y$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $F\to Y$ is a closed immersion, and $v^{-1}(F)=E$ scheme-theoretically. It induces an isomorphism $X\setminus E\simeq Y\setminus F$. The induced map $t:Y\to S$ is proper, and $(Y,\varnothing)$ is a semistable multipointed $k$-curve. At a point $f\in F$ with one preimage $e$, $v$ is an isomorphism on neighbourhoods of $e$ and $f$. At a point with two preimages $e_1,e_2$, the completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is
$$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,f}\cong k[[u]]\times_k k[[v]]\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv),$$
where the maps from the two completed smooth local rings are evaluation at zero [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. In particular the two-point fibres create precisely ordinary nodes. If $D\subset X$ is a reduced closed union of irreducible components [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-irreducible-components] meeting every fibre of $a$ in at most one point, then $v|_D$ is a closed immersion and identifies $D$ with its reduced image in $Y$. Neither $X$ nor $S$ is required to be separated over $k$.

source.place: Tags 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral), 0E26 (lemma-pushout-separated); varieties.tex Tag 09NN (proposition-finite-set-of-points-of-codim-1-in-affine), applied over affine opens of S; curves.tex Tag 0E36 (lemma-complete-local-ring-pushout) and Tag 0C1J (example-glue-points); morphisms.tex Tag 03GN (lemma-image-proper-is-proper). The subcurve-embedding clause is the branch restriction of the fibre-product ring description in 0E25.

proof.text: First verify the affine-neighbourhood hypothesis for pinching. The multipointed-curve hypothesis makes $X$ finitely presented over $k$, hence of finite type. Thus $X$ is Noetherian; every quasi-compact open is Noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components. Fix $f\in F$ and an affine open $V\subseteq S$ containing $b(f)$. The open $X_V=s^{-1}V$ is separated over $k$: its diagonal over $V$ is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $s$, and $X_V\times_VX_V$ is closed in $X_V\times_kX_V$ since the diagonal of the affine $k$-scheme $V$ is closed (on rings, multiplication is surjective). Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, this also makes $X_V$ separated as a scheme. All points of $a^{-1}(f)$ lie in $X_V$. Their local rings are Noetherian of dimension at most one: chains in their spectra are chains of specializations in the one-dimensional scheme $X$. Apply the common-affine-neighbourhood node to $X_V$ and this finite set. This does not assert that $X$ is separated over $k$.

source.place: Tag 09NN (proposition-finite-set-of-points-of-codim-1-in-affine), applied over an affine open of S

proof.text: The map $a$ is integral: on finite discrete spectra it is induced by the diagonal maps $k\to k^r$, $r=1$ or $2$, which are finite modules. The Ferrand node now gives $Y=X\amalg_E F$, the cartesian square, the closed immersion $F\hookrightarrow Y$, the complement isomorphism, and the quotient topology. Since $a$ is surjective, every point of $F$ is already the image of a point of $X$, so $v$ is surjective. Its affine charts have rings $P=A\times_C B$, where $B=k^m$, $C=k^r$, $A\twoheadrightarrow C$ is evaluation on the indicated points of $E$, and $B\hookrightarrow C$ repeats coordinates according to $a$. The pushout property supplies $t$ from $s$ and $b$, and supplies the compatible structural map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.

Let $W\subseteq Y$ be any affine open. The morphisms $v$, $F\to Y$ and $E\to Y$ are affine, so evaluating the structure-sheaf formula of the Ferrand node on $W$ gives $\mathcal O_Y(W)=P=A\times_CB$, where $A=\mathcal O_X(v^{-1}W)$, $B=k^m$ and $C=k^r$ are the rings of the affine schemes $v^{-1}W$, $F\cap W$ and $E\cap v^{-1}W$. Here $A\to C$ is onto by the closed-immersion definition, and $B\to C$ repeats coordinates according to $a$; this is the form of the charts in the preceding step, now for every affine open. On $W$ the map $P\to A$ is injective, because $B\to C$ is injective, and $A/P\cong C/B$ as $P$-modules. This is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. Choose lifts $h_1,\ldots,h_d\in A$ of a $k$-basis of $C/B$. For any $h\in A$, subtract a $k$-linear combination of the $h_i$ to leave an element of $P$. As the scalar copy of $k$ lies in $P$, the finite list $1,h_1,\ldots,h_d$ generates $A$ as a $P$-module. As $W$ was an arbitrary affine open, the affine morphism $v$ is finite by the definition. The cartesian square from the preceding step gives $v^{-1}(F)=E$ with its scheme structure.

source.place: Tag 0E25, structure sheaf as fibre product evaluated on an arbitrary affine open; explicit finite-module argument

proof.text: Apply the finite-type clause of the Ferrand node over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: this base is Noetherian, and $X,E,F$ are of finite type over $k$. Hence $Y/k$ is locally of finite type. The quotient of $X\amalg F$ is quasi-compact: pull an open cover back to this finite union of quasi-compact schemes, take a finite subcover there, and use surjectivity. Thus $Y/k$ is of finite type and is Noetherian. Each finite-type affine $k$-algebra is finitely presented by the Noetherian finite-presentation node. Its Noetherian topological space makes $Y$ quasi-separated, so these local presentations and quasi-compactness show that $Y/k$ is finitely presented.

The map $b:F\to S$ is separated by the affine-source separatedness node, since $F$ is affine. The map $s$ is separated by properness. Apply the relative separatedness clause of the Ferrand node with base $S$ to obtain separatedness of $t$. Since $Y/k$ is locally of finite type, clause (a) of finite-type cancellation applied to $Y\to S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $t$ locally of finite type, without a finiteness condition on $S$. Finally $s$ is universally closed and $v$ is surjective. Apply the universally-closed-image node to $s=t v$; with the two properties just verified its last sentence says precisely that $t$ is proper.

For a singleton fibre $a^{-1}(f)=\{e\}$, remove from $Y$ the images of all the other points of $F$. These are closed, and the Ferrand node identifies the restricted square as the pushout of $X$ with the other pinched fibres removed and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ along $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose latter map is an isomorphism. Its pushout is therefore just that open part of $X$. This proves the neighbourhood-isomorphism assertion and shows this point stays smooth.

source.place: Tag 0E25, compatibility with restriction to opens and the pushout universal property

proof.text: Fix now $f\in F$. Remove the other points of $F$ and choose an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}P$ of $f$ in this open. Write $v^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $a^{-1}(f)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_r\}$, so $P=A\times_{k^r}k$. All these rings are finite $P$-modules: $A$ by step 3, $k$ as a quotient, and $k^r$ as a finite sum of that quotient. Also $P$ is Noetherian by step 4. Complete at the maximal ideal of $f$ the exact sequence $0\to P\to A\oplus k\to k^r\to0$, whose last arrow is evaluation minus the diagonal and is onto because $A\to k^r$ is onto. Exactness of finite-module completion identifies $\widehat{P_f}$ with the kernel after completion. The finite-extension-completion node identifies the completion of $A$ with $\prod_i\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,e_i}$, compatibly with the induced local maps; the completions of $k$ and $k^r$ are themselves, since the maximal ideal of $f$ acts by zero. The maps to $k^r$ are their residue maps. Componentwise multiplication therefore gives the ring isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,f}\cong (\prod_i\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,e_i})\times_{k^r}k$. This is the calculation of 0E36, now with every completion comparison cited.

For each pinched point $e_i$, take a smooth open neighbourhood in $X$. The smooth-over-field regularity node makes its local ring $R_i$ regular and Noetherian. It has dimension one: it has dimension at most one by the specialization-chain argument of step 1, and a generic point of an irreducible component containing the closed point $e_i$ is distinct from $e_i$ (every component has dimension one), giving a strict chain of length one in $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$. Completion preserves regularity and dimension by the two completion nodes. The completion-mod-power node with $N=1$ identifies the completed residue field with $R_i/\mathfrak m_i=k$. For every $N$ the same node gives $\widehat R_i/\mathfrak m_i^N\widehat R_i\cong R_i/\mathfrak m_i^N$ through $\pi^\wedge_N$, so the canonical map from $\widehat R_i$ to its own $\mathfrak m_i\widehat R_i$-adic completion is $(x)\mapsto(\pi^\wedge_N(x))_N$, the identity of $\varprojlim_NR_i/\mathfrak m_i^N$; thus $\widehat R_i$ is complete for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_i\widehat R_i$. The coefficient map $k\to\widehat R_i$ induces the identity on the residue field $k$. A generator of the maximal ideal exists by the definition of a dimension-one regular local ring. Apply the complete-coefficient-coordinates node with $d=1$ to this generator. It gives a complete local $k$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat R_i\cong k[[t_i]]$ carrying the residue map to evaluation at zero.

source.place: Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), clause (2); varieties.tex Tag 056S; more-algebra.tex Tags 07NY and 07NV

proof.text: For $r=2$, steps 7--8 give $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,f}\cong k[[u]]\times_k k[[v]]$. The homomorphism $k[[u,v]]\to k[[u]]\times_k k[[v]]$ sends $h$ to $(h(u,0),h(0,v))$. Its image consists of all pairs with equal constant coefficient: a pair $(p,q)$ is the image of $p(u)+q(v)-p(0)$. Its kernel consists of series with no coefficient on either axis, equivalently multiples of $uv$. It therefore induces $k[[u,v]]/(uv)\cong k[[u]]\times_k k[[v]]$. In particular this point is an ordinary node. Together with step 6 and the complement isomorphism, this accounts for every point of $Y$ and creates no other singularities.

source.place: Tag 0E36 and the ordinary-node model; explicit power-series coefficient calculation

proof.text: It remains to check the dimension clause and the geometric-fibre clause of semistability. The structure map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ has the single fibre $Y$, and its geometric fibre is $Y\times_k\bar k$ for a chosen algebraic closure $\iota:k\to\bar k$. Since $\bar k$ is algebraic over $\iota(k)$ and $k$ is algebraically closed, the minimal polynomial of each element of $\bar k$ is linear, so $\iota$ is an isomorphism; hence the geometric fibres of $X$ and $Y$ are $X$ and $Y$ over $k$, up to this isomorphism. The semistability hypothesis thus says that every point of $X$ is smooth over $k$ or an ordinary double point, and it suffices to prove the same for $Y$ over $k$. The points of $F$ are closed, so every non-closed point of $Y$, and every closed point outside $F$, lies in $Y\setminus F\simeq X\setminus E$, where the property is inherited from $X$. At $f\in F$ the point is smooth by step 6 or an ordinary double point by step 9. Pure dimension one: $X$ is Noetherian of pure dimension one. Each irreducible component $Z$ of $X$ has its generic point outside the closed points $E$; by the quotient topology of the Ferrand node, $v(Z)$ is closed, since its saturation $v^{-1}v(Z)$ adds only finitely many closed points of $E$ and its trace on $F$ is finite. Distinct generic points remain distinct, so the $v(Z)$ are precisely the irreducible components of $Y$. A proper closed subset of $Z$ is a finite set of closed points (a Noetherian space of dimension one); pulling a proper closed subset of $v(Z)$ back to $Z$ shows it is finite as well, so $v(Z)$, which still has its generic point and a distinct closed point, has dimension one. The finite presentation was checked in step 4; flatness over a field follows because every vector space is free. The empty marking is finitely presented, flat, etale and contained in the smooth locus vacuously. These are all clauses of the semistable multipointed-curve definition.

source.place: Tag 0E36 with Example 0C1J; geometric fibre over the algebraically closed field k itself; explicit verification of the multipointed-curve clauses

proof.text: Finally let $W\subseteq Y$ be any affine open, with $\mathcal O_Y(W)=P=A\times_C B$ as in step 3, and write $D\cap\operatorname{Spec}A=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Given $\bar h\in A/I$, choose $h\in A$. Choose one scalar for each fibre of $a$: use $h(e)$ if that fibre meets $D$, and use zero otherwise. This is consistent because each fibre meets $D$ in at most one point. These scalars form $b\in B$. For each indicated $e_j\notin D$, choose $q_j\in I$ with $q_j(e_j)=1$; this exists since $I$ is not contained in its maximal ideal, followed by scaling in $k$. Since $A\to C$ is onto, choose $\delta_j\in A$ with evaluations one at $e_j$ and zero at the other indicated points. Add to $h$ the sum of $(b(a(e_j))-h(e_j))q_j\delta_j$ over $e_j\notin D$. This changes no class in $A/I$, changes the desired residues exactly, and leaves residues on $D$ untouched. The resulting $h_1$ satisfies $(h_1,b)\in P$. Thus $P\to A/I$ is onto. The affine criterion for a closed immersion proves that $D\to Y$ is a closed immersion. It identifies $D$ with its image with its given reduced scheme structure, since $D$ is reduced. When $E=F=\varnothing$, the pushout is $X$, the maps and all clauses are identities or vacuous; when $D$ is empty the argument has the zero ring $A/I$.

source.place: Tag 0E25, fibre-product rings on every affine open; explicit residue interpolation for the branch restriction
